title: U Brucculinu
canon: A baroque hilltown in southeastern Sicily, 1972 — Modica is the model. Santo Calvino, a Brooklyn boxer and Vietnam veteran ('u brucculinu' — the Brooklynite), returns to his ancestral town for a quiet life, marries the fierce Elena, and is forced into a public reckoning with her brother, the padrone Don Lino Gradi, over her withheld million-lire dowry — which Santo wins and then burns. CANON.md is a stub; names and beats are provisional from the pitch deck.
look: 1972 Sicily shot like 1970s Italian cinema: Eastmancolor warmth gone slightly faded, heavy 35mm grain, honey-colored Val di Noto limestone. Day frames run on the sun alone — hard high Mediterranean light, dust haze, blown pale-stone highlights, deep doorway shadow, no fill. Dusk and night frames run on the town's own practicals: streetlamps, lit windows, fire. Every frame is full-bleed, edge to edge — the existing set kept baking in pillarbox bars.
note: Six shots mined from the NotebookLM pitch deck (04-documents/slide_deck_u_brucculinu_v001.pdf), which is the only story source — CANON.md and the vault's 03-setting/02-themes/07-locations notes are stubs. The deck fixes 1972 Sicily, protagonist Santo Calvino (Brooklyn boxing legend, Vietnam vet), wife Elena, padrone Don Lino Gradi, the million-lire dowry, the threshing-yard brawl and the dowry burned in the threshing engine's firebox; deck working title is 'Il Silenzio del Calvino' while the vault titles the property 'U Bruculinu' (single c) — spelling and names need Marco's ruling. Modica-panorama.jpg (real photograph) anchors the town's look. CAST CONTINUITY WARNINGS: the two existing love-interest stills are two different faces (02-love-interest.png vs 09-ubr-02-love.jpg) — this spec refs 02-love-interest.png as Elena and drops the other; Santo has NO established face (the hilltown still is from behind, the fight still's faces are uncontrolled), so prompts describe him and ref only his wardrobe — picking a canonical Santo is Marco's call. Failures avoided: baked-in pillarbox bars (02/03/04/u-bruculinu-hilltown), gibberish poster text (03), off-canon Northern Gothic church with vignette borders (08). 2026-07-16 STORY LAW pass: six story shots appended (caught-courting, the-tribute-cart, the-tiger-held, a-calvino-and-a-coward, the-open-hand, fire-in-the-terraces) — the beats between arrival and the dowry burning, mined from the pitch deck: forbidden courtship caught, Lino's tribute system, Santo's restraint read as cowardice, Elena's 'a Calvino and a coward' accusation, the public dowry demand on the San Giorgio steps, and the retaliation fire. Elena shown visibly with child in a-calvino-and-a-coward per the deck quote 'the father of this my son' — that read needs Marco's ruling. Existing six shots untouched.

stills.prompt: A man walks alone up a white gravel road toward Modica, a baroque hilltown in southeastern Sicily, in the summer of 1972, seen from behind. Santo Calvino, mid-forties, a boxer's shoulders under a sweat-marked white shirt with the sleeves rolled, brown trousers, a battered leather suitcase in one hand — an American walking back into his grandfather's town. The road switchbacks up through dry terraces, olive trees and low dry-stone walls, and above it the town climbs the hillside: honey-colored limestone houses stacked shoulder to shoulder, a baroque church dome and bell tower at the crown. Daylight runs the frame: late-afternoon sun low from the west, the single light source, raking long shadows off the olive trees, dust hanging gold in the air, the pale stone blowing out hot. Full-bleed frame edge to edge, no black bars, no letterbox. Wide anamorphic composition, 35mm film still, faded Eastmancolor warmth, heavy natural grain, cinematic. No text, no watermark.

stills.prompt: Evening in the main piazza of Modica, Sicily, summer 1972. A row of old men sit on wooden chairs outside a small bar beneath its canvas awning — flat caps, suspenders, shirtsleeves — one reading a newspaper, the rest watching the square with the patience of men who have watched it for fifty years. The light is dusk's own: the sun is gone, the sky holds a warm afterglow that washes the whole square soft amber, and the bar's single doorway bulb throws the one warm pool across the men's chairs. stills.prompt: A bare-knuckle fight in a threshing yard on a dry hillside farm outside Modica, Sicily, summer 1972. Santo Calvino, mid-forties, a Brooklyn boxer's stance, white shirt torn and grey with chaff dust, stands over Don Lino Gradi, the padrone — heavier, in a cream linen suit gone filthy, down on one knee in the straw. Around them a ring of farmhands and villagers in caps and work clothes keeps its distance against wheat sacks, a wooden cart and the iron bulk of a threshing machine; dust and chaff hang thick in the air. Daylight runs the frame: hard early-afternoon sun almost overhead, the single source, bouncing violent and bright off the pale threshing floor into every shadow, the dust haze glowing, highlights blowing out. stills.prompt: Sunset in a threshing yard outside Modica, Sicily, summer 1972. Santo Calvino — mid-forties, torn dusty white shirt, a boxer's build — stands at the open iron firebox door of a steam threshing engine and feeds a thick stack of lire banknotes into the flames. Beside him Elena, dark curls, floral dress, watches with her chin lifted, proud; a few steps back Don Lino Gradi, the padrone in his rumpled cream linen suit, has dropped to his knees in the straw, aghast. A loose ring of villagers and farmhands stands in silhouette against the last light. Two sources of light and no others: the deep orange sunset sky behind the hills rims every figure, and the firebox throws a hard hot glow forward onto Santo's arm, his face, the burning notes and Elena's dress, sparks and chaff drifting through its beam. Deep shadow everywhere the fire does not reach. Full-bleed frame edge to edge, no black bars, no letterbox. stills.prompt: Night in a narrow stepped lane of Modica, Sicily, summer 1972. Santo Calvino — mid-forties, a boxer's shoulders in a white shirt with the sleeves rolled, brown trousers — and Elena — around thirty, dark curls loose, a floral-print dress — stand caught close together at a small stone wall fountain, alone, unchaperoned, against every rule of the town. Directly above them a pair of wooden shutters has just banged open and an old woman in black leans out staring down; two more windows further along the lane are lighting up. Elena has half turned toward the noise, chin lifted, defiant; Santo still holds her hand and does not let go. The night runs on practicals only: one amber streetlamp on an iron wall bracket above the fountain, the warm tungsten spill of the waking windows raking down the worn stone steps, everything beyond falling to black. stills.prompt: Midday in the main piazza of Modica, Sicily, summer 1972. Two of Don Lino Gradi's men in dark trousers and sweat-stained shirts heave a poor farmer's grain sacks from his mule cart onto a flatbed truck — tribute being taken, not trade. The farmer, sixty, stands rigid beside his emptied cart with his flat cap crushed in both hands, his young son gripping the mule's halter. A few steps away Don Lino Gradi, the padrone — heavier, immaculate in a cream linen suit — watches without expression beside a black Lancia sedan. Across the flagstones the old men outside the bar have all turned their chairs and faces away; a woman pulls her child indoors. Daylight runs the frame: hard noon Mediterranean sun almost straight overhead, the single source, crushing shadows to small black pools underfoot, the pale limestone facades and flagstones blowing out hot, dust in the air. No legible signage anywhere. Full-bleed frame edge to edge, no black bars, no letterbox. Wide anamorphic composition, 35mm film still, faded Eastmancolor warmth, heavy natural grain, cinematic. stills.notes: STORY LAW: the violence Santo swore to contain, shown by NOT happening. stills.prompt: Market morning in a narrow street of Modica, Sicily, summer 1972. A big enforcer in a dark waistcoat and rolled sleeves has just upended Santo Calvino's market basket at his feet — tomatoes and onions scattered and burst across the sunlit flagstones — and stands square in his face, laughing, daring him. Santo Calvino, mid-forties, a boxer's shoulders in a white shirt with the sleeves rolled, brown trousers, stands utterly still over the ruined produce: fists clenched white at his sides, not raised, jaw set, eyes level at the man. Around them the market has stopped — women with net bags, a fishmonger at his stall, old men in caps — every face watching, some already curling into contempt at the American who will not fight. Daylight runs the frame: hard mid-morning sun slicing down the narrow street from one side, the single source, hard black shadow filling the opposite wall, the crushed tomatoes glistening in the light, no fill. No legible signage anywhere. Full-bleed frame edge to edge, no black bars, no letterbox. Wide anamorphic composition, 35mm film still, faded Eastmancolor warmth, heavy natural grain, cinematic. No text, no watermark.

stills.prompt: Night inside a small stone-walled kitchen in Modica, Sicily, summer 1972. Elena — around thirty, dark curls, a floral housedress, visibly with child, one hand resting on her rounded belly — has flung the heavy front door wide open onto the dark lane and stands pointing out through it, arm rigid, her face bitter and burning, mid-sentence. At the plank table Santo Calvino — mid-forties, a boxer's shoulders in an undershirt, suspenders down — grips the table edge with both hands, knuckles white, head bowed, not yet moving toward the door he is being sent through. On the table between them sits an unopened envelope of lire. The night runs on practicals only: a single bare tungsten bulb hanging low over the table, the dying orange embers of the hearth catching one side of Elena's dress, the open doorway a slab of black. On the wide stone steps Santo Calvino — mid-forties, a boxer's shoulders in a pressed white shirt buttoned to the collar, brown Sunday trousers — stands one step below Don Lino Gradi, the padrone, heavier, in a cream linen suit and hat, and holds out one open empty palm between them: a debt being called, in front of everyone. Elena — around thirty, dark curls pinned up, a floral Sunday dress — stands at Santo's shoulder, chin high. Behind Lino two of his men have gone tense; the congregation — women in black lace veils, men in caps and Sunday jackets — has frozen fanned across the staircase, every eye on the open hand. Daylight runs the frame: hard late-morning sun raking across the church's carved limestone front, the single source, blowing the pale stone out hot and dropping the portal behind them into black shadow, no fill. stills.prompt: Night on a terraced olive smallholding on the hillside below Modica, Sicily, summer 1972. A line of fire is eating along the dry grass of one terrace and climbing into two old olive trees — a fire set deliberately, burning in a straight line along the dry-stone wall. Santo Calvino — mid-forties, boxer's shoulders, an undershirt soaked with sweat and ash, brown trousers — beats at the flame line with a soaked sack, mid-swing, embers whirling around him; Elena — dark curls loose, a shawl over her nightdress — hauls a sloshing tin bucket up the terrace steps toward him. Across the black gorge behind them the lights of Modica stack up the far hill, warm windows and a string of amber streetlamps, distant and indifferent. The fire is the only light on them — hard orange, flickering, throwing their shadows huge across the dry-stone wall — with deep black night beyond its reach.
